Dataspace Management

Know which datasets get data, and which ones are yours to change

Dataspace Management shows your default, Frequent Search and system datasets on one page, for admins who govern data across business units.

See it in the design

Status and owner on every row

Each dataset shows if it receives data and who manages it. System and Frequent Search datasets say why you cannot change them.

Design preview with sample data. The final product may differ. Hover the window to pause it; the corner button opens it larger.

The problem today

Your datasets sit in tabs that work differently

Two tabs, two layouts

Default and system datasets show different columns and different edit panels. You learn the page twice.

Frequent Search is missing

Frequent Search is a dataspace, but its datasets are not on the page. You cannot see them next to the rest.

Two ways to stop writes

Default and system datasets each have their own dialog to turn writes on or off.

Use case

A platform admin checks what is theirs to change

what happened

Many datasets, one question

The admin routes logs into datasets, one per business domain. They need to find datasets with no data, and see which ones they can change.

what the page shows

Status and owner

A rail with Default, Frequent Search and System, each with its count. One dataset shows "No data yet". Managed by shows User or Predefined. Frequent Search says it cannot be created, edited or disabled here.

what the admin knows

What is theirs

Which datasets get data, which ones are theirs to change, and why the rest are locked.
